newsitem.title: USA: Crews search for tanks in Houston Ship Channel.
newsitem.headline: Crews search for tanks in Houston Ship Channel.

text.p: Crews continued to search Friday for six large tanks that sank in the Houston Ship Channel, restricting traffic in the waterway used by tankers shipping crude to local refineries, officials said.
The tanks loaded with zinc bromide fell overboard on Thursday after the barge they were on was swept by the wake of a passing ship, prompting restrictions on shipping through the channel.
"We're still looking for those sunken tanks. We haven't found them yet," U.S. Coast Guard Lt. Diane Hauser said.

The accident delayed traffic and closed the channel to deep-draft ships between mileposts 52 and 56, where a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers side-sweep sonar ship is searching for the tanks. Barges, tows and shallow-draft ships are still allowed through the area.

Deep-draft tankers can still reach refineries near Galveston and Texas City, but there is no deep-draft traffic into the Port of Houston along the ship channel, the waterway linking Houston's refinery row with the Gulf of Mexico.
